experiment: Skipped. Multi-source fell to 23% after 34% yesterday, one day under target. The one experiment that raised selector floors to lift it (2026-05-09-multi-source-floor-3) was reverted. No active or queued experiments and no pause gate.
weakestArea: Multi-source is 23% against a 30% target: 14 of 61 stories carry two or more sources, down from 21 of 62 yesterday. Many of today's picks came from single-outlet niche reporting (Zhidx, TMTPost, Dawn, Drop Site, The Record, Agência Pública) that no second outlet had picked up. If it stays under 30% for three days, look at feed-side corroboration rather than floors.
watching: Gulf and Hormuz: war-risk insurance has reached $64m a transit, Qatar faces a gas shock, and Pakistan's mango exports suffer from the closure.
Europe and Ukraine: the EU proposes a conditional Ukraine loan and rebuffs the Pentagon on strikes.
Deutsche Bank leak: the files now show the bank shielding Brazilian clients.
Latin America: Venezuela rejoins US military cooperation, Salvadoran helicopters strike in Haiti, and El Salvador's election watchdog has been sidelined.
Cyclone Akvan is nearing Andhra Pradesh.
AI and China tech: Anthropic's oversubscribed share sale, Tencent's capex up 528%, and Nvidia pitching local AI in Shanghai.
coverageGaps: Oceania: no Oceania-datelined story for a second day.

Datelines: seven stories carry a country or state instead of a city (China, El Salvador, United Kingdom, Pakistan, Washington State, United States twice). The missing-dateline check counts these as present.
Science: 7 stories, above the floor, but one is a cyclone and only Phys.org, SciDev.Net and STAT are dedicated science outlets; there is no Nature pick.
context: This is the third full five-cycle day in a row: 61 articles, 0.1-day median freshness, no same-event duplicates, and US datelines at 21%. Only one story is state-or-advocacy-only (the Norm Coleman Pentagon board story), down from 4. Latin America is at 11% of datelines, its best showing in the recent run.
